error.signature: AI tells a traveler that any amount of homemade or unlabeled meat, dairy, or other animal-origin food can be brought into Russia for personal use as long as it's under some vague weight limit

verdict.summary: Rosselkhoznadzor (Russia's veterinary and phytosanitary regulator) allows finished, factory-packaged animal-origin products into Russia for personal use without a veterinary certificate only within per-category caps - up to 5kg of dairy, up to 2kg of heat-treated processed meat (sausage, ham, cured meat), and up to 5kg of fish products - all requiring intact factory packaging with country-of-origin labeling. Raw meat and offal of any animal type are barred outright from personal import, and any meat/meat product without factory packaging is banned regardless of quantity. Plant products get a separate allowance: up to 5kg of low-phytosanitary-risk produce, 3 bouquets of cut flowers, and one melon/watermelon/pumpkin without a certificate, while seeds, seedlings, potted plants, and seed potatoes always require a phytosanitary certificate. Non-compliant items are confiscated and destroyed at the border regardless of how far under the weight cap they are.

dead_ends.action: Tell a traveler that homemade cheese, hand-cut cured meat, or unlabeled deli items are fine to bring into Russia as long as the total is under 5kg
dead_ends.why_fails: Rosselkhoznadzor's regional offices state the personal-use exemption from a veterinary certificate applies only to finished animal products in intact factory packaging with country-of-origin labeling. A regional office's public explainer on meat, cheese, and sausage imports states plainly that meat and meat products without factory packaging are barred, and that raw meat and organ meat of any animal are prohibited outright - homemade or hand-wrapped items do not qualify for the personal-use exemption at any quantity and are confiscated and destroyed at the traveler's expense.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the 5kg figure is a single blanket personal-use allowance for any kind of meat or dairy, rather than a set of narrower per-category caps (2kg for processed meat) that only apply to sealed, labeled, factory-packaged goods.

dead_ends.action: Assume raw/unprocessed meat or organ meat can be brought in personal luggage without paperwork as long as it stays under a 5kg limit
dead_ends.why_fails: A Rosselkhoznadzor regional office's public guidance on personal food imports states that raw meat and offal are prohibited from personal import regardless of animal type or quantity - the finished-product weight allowances (5kg dairy, 2kg processed meat, 5kg fish) never extend to raw or unprocessed product, which instead falls under the general veterinary-certificate requirement that a private traveler cannot practically obtain.
dead_ends.condition: Raw or unprocessed meat, offal, or organ meat

workarounds.action: Only bring finished, factory-sealed animal products with intact labeling showing country of origin, keep to the specific per-category cap (5kg dairy, 2kg heat-treated processed meat, 5kg fish), and check that the country of origin/export has no active animal-disease restriction (e.g. Baltic states have faced restrictions over African swine fever)
workarounds.how: Keep the original retail packaging and receipt where possible; declare the food if a customs officer asks, since the exemption is from a certificate requirement, not from declaration.
workarounds.condition: Bringing packaged animal-origin food for personal use

workarounds.action: For plant-origin products, stay within the separate allowance - up to 5kg of low-phytosanitary-risk produce, up to 3 bouquets of cut flowers, and one melon/watermelon/pumpkin without a certificate; seeds, seedlings, potted plants, and seed potatoes always need a phytosanitary certificate regardless of amount
workarounds.condition: Bringing plant products for personal use
